principles: Mode selection changes automation depth, never truth or authority semantics.
Conservative mode must remain useful and safe without server authority.
Authority-Verified mode must require explicit server-authority evidence before any stronger integration claim.
Full Autopilot must be bounded, observable, cancellable, and resumable rather than an unbounded loop.
Existing dispatch_auto, dispatch_review, validation, and merge_plan primitives are the source of behavior; autopilot orchestrates them.
drivers: User wants unattended host-to-host development that can complete intent, but without false completion claims.
Existing Lattice dispatch stack already has policy and Claude runner; this story should compose it, not rebuild it.
High-risk lifecycle/production wording requires explicit preMortem, tests, and no-overclaim docs.

options.name: single-big-autopilot-switch
pros: Fast to document as one command
cons: Risks accidental auto-merge or productionDone overclaim

options.name: three-policy-modes-on-shared-orchestrator
pros: Conservative mode can ship safely first
Authority and full loop reuse the same state records and gates
cons: Requires careful smoke tests for each mode

options.name: docs-only-host-native-delegation
cons: Does not deliver requested unattended Lattice CLI development loop

rationale: This option gives the user the requested three autopilot modes while keeping Conservative safe by default and making stronger automation depend on explicit authority evidence and bounded stop conditions.

preMortem.scenario: Autopilot claims production completion from local receipt
preMortem.trigger: A local dispatch receipt or host-native transcript is treated as server authority proof.
preMortem.consequence: Lattice would tell the user work is productionDone without external authority verification.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep receiptVerified=false/productionDone=false by default; require explicit fake/live server authority receipt in Authority-Verified tests.

preMortem.scenario: Full autopilot loops forever or spends unbounded resources
preMortem.trigger: Validation keeps failing and auto-fix retries have no hard stop.
preMortem.consequence: Unattended mode burns time, budget, or agent capacity without clear user-visible stop.
preMortem.mitigation: Require maxIterations, maxRuntimeMinutes, maxBudgetUSD, stopOnConflict, and stopOnScopeViolation; smoke test maxIterations stop.

preMortem.trigger: Orchestrator widens allowedPaths, commandAllowlist, or host selection after policy check.
preMortem.consequence: A host could modify files outside the user-authorized scope.
preMortem.mitigation: Bind every dispatch through dispatch_auto policy check and test refusal for widened paths/commands.

preMortem.scenario: Host-native delegation becomes opaque prompt-only execution
preMortem.trigger: Codex asks Claude CLI to work but no transcript/receipt/path evidence is required.
preMortem.consequence: User cannot audit what happened and Lattice cannot safely review or merge.
preMortem.mitigation: Host-native mode outputs required handoff pack, receipt path, transcript expectation, and treats missing evidence as needs_receipt.

preMortem.scenario: Main merge happens from automation despite unresolved conflict
preMortem.trigger: Authority-Verified or Full Autopilot treats accepted_local as mergeable to main.
preMortem.consequence: Existing worktree/branch safety could be violated and user changes overwritten.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep main merge gated by allowMainMerge plus authority evidence; conflict state produces repair task and stops.
